content.text: I want to explore a slack experience where I ask clanker that I want to buy shorts like this (image for ref) and it presents me a carousel of shorts that are similar to the one I refered. what are the components here that I'd hv to get right first of all and feasibility of this experience when using slack

input.input: text(await tools.web__run({search_query:[{q:"site.docs.slack.dev Block Kit carousel cards image section actions"},{"q":"site.docs.slack.dev handling user interaction acknowledge 3 seconds"},{"q":"site.docs.slack.dev files private download authorization files read"}],response_length:"long"}));

content.text:
Slack supports this experience natively today, including an actual horizontal carousel.

1. **Carousel exists.** Slack released `card` and `carousel` blocks on April 16, 2026. A carousel contains **1–10 cards**, with horizontal scrolling and built-in navigation. Supported surfaces are messages and App Home, so the results can sit directly in the conversation. [Release announcement](https://docs.slack.dev/changelog/2026/04/16/block-kit-new-blocks/), [carousel reference](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/blocks/carousel-block/), [surfaces index](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/blocks/).

2. **Product cards fit well.** Each can contain a hero image, title, subtitle, short body, and **up to 3 buttons**. Title/subtitle are limited to 150 characters each; body to 200. Card size cannot be configured. Suggested mapping: image; product name; price + retailer; one sentence explaining visual similarity; buttons for **View product**, **More like this**, and **Save**. [Card reference](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/blocks/card-block/).

3. **Image input is straightforward.** For app DMs, subscribe to `message.im` with `im:history`; download the reference image using a token with `files:read`. Private Slack image URLs require a Bearer authorization header, so sending the private URL directly to an external search provider will generally not work. Fetch bytes in the backend, then send only the necessary image data. A modal upload flow is also available via `file_input`, but an ordinary message attachment is the more natural entry point here. [DM events](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/message.im/), [file permissions](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/scopes/files.read/), [private file access](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/objects/file-object/), [modal file input](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/block-elements/file-input-element/).

4. **Interactive refinement needs state and fast acknowledgement.** Button callbacks must be acknowledged within **3 seconds**; search/ranking should continue asynchronously. Store the search session, selected product, constraints and message timestamp. `chat.update` can replace the bot’s carousel for “cheaper,” “different colour,” or “show more.” Modals can gather size/budget, but must open from a user interaction using its short-lived `trigger_id`; carousel blocks are not listed for modal surfaces. [Interactions](https://docs.slack.dev/interactivity/handling-user-interaction/), [message updates](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.update/), [modals](https://docs.slack.dev/surfaces/modals/).

5. **Recommended first UX:** user sends photo + request → quick “Finding similar shorts” message → **5 ranked product cards** → conversational refinements in the same thread. Use App Home later for saved items/history. Render product images from publicly hosted `image_url`s or authorized Slack files, with alt text. [Image sources](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/block-elements/image-element/), [App Home](https://docs.slack.dev/surfaces/app-home/).

This is verified platform feasibility from current official documentation; rendering in Clanker’s actual workspace and clients remains untested. The major engineering uncertainty is product discovery, visual ranking, and reliable price/stock data, rather than Slack’s carousel UI.
